The splash is released only when `isAppearanceLoaded` flips on *this* `MainViewModel` instance. That holds today because `getViewModel<MainViewModel>()` and the `koinViewModel()` call inside `App()` resolve the same `ViewModelStoreOwner` with the default key, so they return the same cached instance — but this is an implicit, load-bearing contract. It also means the splash has no upper bound of its own: the only release paths are `MainViewModel`'s internal 2s watchdog (`APPEARANCE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`) and the stream's first emission. If that watchdog is ever altered/removed, or if the Compose side starts resolving a different owner (e.g. `App()` wrapped in a scoped `NavHost`/`ViewModelStoreOwner`), the condition can stay `true` indefinitely and the user is stuck on the splash with no fallback.

Consider adding an Activity-owned bound (e.g. a local flag released by a `lifecycleScope`-launched delay/hard timeout) so any divergence degrades to a brief splash instead of a permanent hang.
